Alright, Thursday is here and the news cycle is absolutely wild. Midterms shook everything up, tech is correcting, and some truly bizarre stuff is happening globally. Grab a coffee, let's dive in.

***

**Money Talk**

-   **IRS tweaks 2027 tax rules, giving some breathing room.**
    Good news for your future self (or your heirs): the IRS is boosting estate and gift tax exemptions, plus upping federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for 2027. Inflation adjustments hitting different, I guess. [S1][S2]
-   **Nasdaq tanks, VIX surges on AI regulation fears.**
    Wall Street’s fear gauge hasn't moved this much since April, and it's all thanks to a "blue wave" post-midterms. Tech and AI stocks, including Musk's SpaceX, are getting hammered as investors brace for tougher scrutiny and regulation on everything from data centers to algorithms. Ouch. [S3][S6][S11][S50]
-   **Bank of England hikes rates for the first time in three years.**
    In a move most analysts saw coming, the BoE lifted interest rates to 4% from 3.75%. Inflation's still doing its thing, so don't be surprised if another hike comes knocking soon. The cost of living crisis just got a bit more… crispy. [S8][S13]
-   **Blue Origin delays New Glenn launch (again).**
    Jeff Bezos's space venture won't be flying its New Glenn rocket until January 2027. Apparently, rebuilding a launch pad damaged by an explosion in May is a bit tougher than anticipated. Space is hard, launches are harder. [S5]
-   **Democrats eye Trump's energy deals for upcoming investigations.**
    With a freshly blue Congress, Democrats are sharpening their knives for Trump-era energy interventions, especially in Venezuela and those mineral deals. Expect some juicy oversight hearings and potential headaches for anyone tied to those projects. [S4]

**World Lore**

-   **Europe hit by coordinated bomb threats, raising hybrid war fears.**
    Over 25 flights across Europe were disrupted, forced into emergency landings or diversions, due to a wave of hoax bomb threats. Coming just days after similar alerts, it's raising serious questions about coordinated attacks and potential "hybrid warfare" tactics. Not exactly a relaxing travel season. [S12]
-   **Paraguay's president out amidst bank scandal.**
    Santiago Peña barely had time to resign before Paraguayan lawmakers impeached him. This swift exit follows the collapse of a digital bank tied to his government, which froze millions in savings. Talk about a swift fall from grace. [S21]
-   **US midterm fallout signals shift on Iran war.**
    The "blue wave" didn't just hit domestically; it's got major foreign policy implications. Exit polls suggest Trump's Iran war is deeply unpopular, putting figures like Defense Chief Pete Hegseth on the hot seat and giving Gulf states reason for optimism. Time to pivot? [S31][S32]
-   **Ukraine sees glimmer of hope with Oleshky ceasefire.**
    Amidst the ongoing conflict, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in Oleshky, allowing hundreds of civilians to evacuate. It's a small win, but observers are hoping it could pave the way for more humanitarian missions. Keep your fingers crossed. [S33]
-   **Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to another decade.**
    In a stark reminder of Beijing's grip, pro-democracy leader Joshua Wong was hit with another 10-year prison sentence under the national security law. It's a crushing blow to what was once a vibrant movement. [S25]

**Tech Tea**

-   **AI market gets a midterm hangover as Nasdaq tanks.**
    Well, that didn't take long. Post-election, the Nasdaq plummeted up to 5%, heading for its worst day in 18 months. Investors are officially spooked about the "blue wave" bringing tougher scrutiny and regulation to the AI industry. Meanwhile, OpenAI is still bullish on a 2027 IPO. Bold. [S11][S38][S40][S50][S44]
-   **Claude AI wants to manage your bank account directly.**
    Anthropic's Claude is rolling out a new "Personal Finance" feature that connects directly to your bank and card accounts via Plaid. So now you can ask an LLM, "where did all my money go?" and actually get an answer. What could possibly go wrong? [S49]
-   **US warns of 'ongoing cyber threat' amidst mass industrial hacks.**
    The Feds are sounding the alarm about widespread hacks targeting industrial retail and military freezers. Food, transportation, and healthcare industries are all affected, highlighting a chilling vulnerability in critical infrastructure. Pun intended. [S43]
-   **Meta preps for AI expansion headwinds.**
    Mark Zuckerberg's empire is warning that growing political opposition to data center construction could threaten future AI investments. Communities pushing back against massive infrastructure projects are forcing Meta to rethink its growth strategy. Not every NIMBY wants a supercomputer in their backyard. [S41]
-   **New smart ring aims to control your AI agent with a tap.**
    Forget talking to your phone. Startup Aina is betting on a smart ring that lets you control your autonomous AI agents with a single tap. Because who needs to pull out a phone when you can just look vaguely at your hand? [S53]

**Creator Szn**

-   **AI isn't fixing ad conversion, it's just bloating briefs.**
    Turns out, just because you *can* use AI to generate endless media and creative briefs, doesn't mean you *should*. Agencies are drowning in "brief bloat," and ChatGPT ads are still struggling with conversion rates despite OpenAI's lofty ad revenue targets. More isn't always better. [S58][S59]
-   **Grocery stores are the new media channels, apparently.**
    Move over, TikTok. Marketers are now reimagining the humble grocery store as prime real estate for "retail media," finding new ways to engage you while you're picking up milk. Your weekly shop just got even more surveilled. [S56]
-   **Channel 4 drops 'Married at First Sight UK' after rape allegations.**
    Following two reviews sparked by allegations of rape and sexual misconduct during filming, Channel 4 has pulled the plug on its popular reality show. A stark reminder that content production needs to get its act together. [S15]
-   **Liquid Death already looking for LiveRamp alternatives.**
    In the wake of Publicis acquiring identity graph firm LiveRamp, Liquid Death’s media chief is making moves to ditch them. It seems brands are getting antsy about consolidation in the adtech space, fearing lock-in and higher prices. [S57]
-   **Reddit founder says building social apps is "not cool anymore."**
    Alexis Ohanian, co-founder of Reddit, believes much of the internet is "compromised" and that creating new social media apps isn't where it's at. He's looking for what's next in user-generated content, signaling a potential shift in the digital landscape's hottest sectors. [S51]

**Supply Lines**

-   **Zipline soars to $21B valuation, adding 300 Walmart drone sites.**
    The drone delivery unicorn is expanding aggressively, deepening its partnership with Walmart to roll out hundreds more delivery hubs. That's a huge bet on the future of last-mile logistics, proving that sometimes, the sky's the limit. [S93]
-   **Harbinger raises $240M with FedEx investing.**
    The EV platform startup for trucks and beyond just scored a massive funding round, bringing its total past $650 million. FedEx jumping in as a strategic investor signals serious industry confidence in electrifying fleets and extending their reach beyond just trucks. [S64]
-   **Amazon deploys smart glasses for delivery drivers, swaps Grubhub for Uber Eats.**
    Drivers are getting AR navigation directly in their field of view, aiming for efficiency gains and fewer missed turns. Meanwhile, Prime members can now ditch Grubhub for Uber Eats delivery perks, a major shift in Amazon's food delivery play and a headache for Grubhub. [S70][S89][S90][S91][S92]
-   **Port of Long Beach gears up for record 10 million TEU year.**
    Looks like trade volumes are still kicking, with the Californian port expecting its busiest year ever. Despite all the talk of economic slowdowns, the real-world numbers at the docks tell a different story – goods are still moving, and in huge volumes. [S73]
-   **Maersk posts billions, but investors are not impressed.**
    The ocean giant had a strong quarter across all units, yet its stock tanked over 11% in early trade. Apparently, even printing billions in profits isn't enough to convince the market when the CEO's earnings call goes "on, and on, and on..." [S75]

**Speed Round**

-   Russell Brand found guilty of rape, prison time coming.
-   Bob Dylan popped by the Vatican for a brief chat with Pope Leo.
-   UK might ban smart glasses over creepy, secret filming concerns.
-   France just saw over 600,000 people protest the rising cost of living.
-   A Democrat pulled off a stunning Senate upset in crimson Mississippi.
-   OpenAI's president hints at a 2027 IPO, despite the tech market turbulence.
-   The US Army is enlisting FedEx to modernize its logistics depots.
